target: acceptance 6 — casing and padding resolve rather than refuse. Proven two ways: standard variants resolve positively, and hardened variants reach the payload gate (not the invalid-value branch), which is the only way normalization is observable for a value whose payload is absent.
cmd:
a=$("$PLUGIN_ROOT/scripts/lib/tracker.sh" profile "$FIXTURES/profile/upper_std.md" 2>/dev/null); b=$("$PLUGIN_ROOT/scripts/lib/tracker.sh" profile "$FIXTURES/profile/mixed_std.md" 2>/dev/null); c=$("$PLUGIN_ROOT/scripts/lib/tracker.sh" profile "$FIXTURES/profile/padded_std.md" 2>/dev/null); h1=$(TRACKER_AGENTS_DIR="$PWD/none" "$PLUGIN_ROOT/scripts/lib/tracker.sh" profile "$FIXTURES/profile/upper.md" 2>&1 >/dev/null); h2=$(TRACKER_AGENTS_DIR="$PWD/none" "$PLUGIN_ROOT/scripts/lib/tracker.sh" profile "$FIXTURES/profile/mixed.md" 2>&1 >/dev/null); h3=$(TRACKER_AGENTS_DIR="$PWD/none" "$PLUGIN_ROOT/scripts/lib/tracker.sh" profile "$FIXTURES/profile/padded.md" 2>&1 >/dev/null); pay=$(printf "%s
%s
%s" "$h1" "$h2" "$h3" | grep -c "payload is not installed"); inv=$(printf "%s
%s
%s" "$h1" "$h2" "$h3" | grep -c "invalid profile"); printf '{"a":"%s","b":"%s","c":"%s","payload":%s,"invalid":%s}' "$a" "$b" "$c" "$pay" "$inv"
